You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group number 147, conventionally denoted P-3, with Hall symbol "-P 3". The input cell is hexagonal, with lattice parameters a = b = 6.37236031 Å, c = 6.524608 Å, and interaxial angles α = β = 90.0°, γ = 120.00000322000002°. This cell contains 11 atoms with the composition Eu₁Re₂O₈. Fractional coordinates are used throughout. The input frame and the standard crystallographic frame coincide exactly: the transformation from input to standard coordinates is q_standard = P q_input + s, where P is the identity matrix with diagonal elements 1.0 and off-diagonal elements 0.0, and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). Thus the supplied fractional coordinates are already in the standard setting, and no frame conversion is needed to recover the original geometry.

Within this cell, europium occupies a single crystallographic orbit, the Wyckoff position 1b, with multiplicity 1. Its representative atom sits at fractional coordinates (0.0, 0.0, 0.5), corresponding to the fixed coordinate relation (0, 0, 1/2). This site has no free positional parameters.

Rhenium occupies the Wyckoff position 2d, with multiplicity 2. The representative Re atom is located at (1/3, 2/3, z), with the single independent parameter z = 0.802321; explicitly, the representative fractional coordinates are (0.3333333333333333, 0.6666666666666666, 0.802321). The second Re atom of this orbit is generated by the symmetry operations of P-3 from this representative.

Oxygen is distributed over two independent orbits. The first oxygen orbit is the Wyckoff position 6g, with multiplicity 6 and a fully general coordinate relation (x, y, z). Its representative atom has fractional coordinates (0.145339, 0.36844999999999994, 0.713007), so the three independent parameters are x = 0.145339, y = 0.36844999999999994, and z = 0.713007. The six symmetry-equivalent oxygen atoms of this orbit are generated from this representative by the space-group symmetry.

The second oxygen orbit is the Wyckoff position 2d, with multiplicity 2, sharing the same Wyckoff letter as rhenium but constituting a distinct sublattice. Its representative atom lies at (1/3, 2/3, z) with independent parameter z = 0.068106, that is, at fractional coordinates (0.3333333333333333, 0.6666666666666666, 0.068106). The second oxygen atom of this orbit is generated by symmetry.

All positional values are reported to six decimal places, as indicated by the rounding precision of 6 digits. No precision corrections are required: the list of corrections is empty, so the stated input fractional positions already represent the real input geometry without any displacement adjustments. Together, the Eu 1b site, the Re 2d site, the O 6g site, and the O 2d site account for the full Eu₁Re₂O₈ composition of the 11-atom input cell under P-3 symmetry.
